packet.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty, is the row a numeric limit, report-only monitoring, or something else?
packet.relation_contract: empty numeric limit must be classified before comparison; absence is not a denial

candidate_interpretations.statement: Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR denotes a monitoring/reporting requirement with no numeric effluent limit in that limit slot (permit tables show 'Report' or 'N/A' for that column).

Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR on one limit-type row for a parameter does not mean no numeric limit exists; the same permit and parameter may carry the numeric limit on a sibling row with populated LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.
Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR on WET retest rows denotes pass/fail reporting encoded as 0/1 rather than a concentration limit.

Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows tied to WHEN DISCHARGING or geometric-mean reporting footnotes denote monitoring obligations whose numeric comparison applicability depends on conditions or aggregation not captured in LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.
Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR might reflect missing structured encoding rather than an established non-numeric classification, especially where permit text is not matched in this workspace.

judgment.interpretation: Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is not a uniform semantic class. Workspace permit text (gcc, aztec, farmington) establishes that for matched parameters, empty values in report-average or Report-column slots denote report-only monitoring without a numeric concentration limit in that row, while numeric limits may appear on sibling rows for the same parameter. Structured DMR_COMMENT_TEXT on sources/permit_limits.csv establishes a distinct pass/fail (0/1) category on 12 WET retest rows and signals conditional ('WHEN DISCHARGING') or aggregated (geometric mean) obligations on others. However, no single structured field or reusable rule classifies all 57 empty rows: LIMIT_TYPE_CODE is uniformly ENF, LIMIT_VALUE_TYPE_CODE has no workspace codebook, 18/57 rows have blank DMR_COMMENT_TEXT without permit-text cross-check in the packet, and discharge-occurrence evidence needed for conditional rows is absent. The obligation therefore cannot be resolved to one answer (numeric limit, report-only, or a single alternative) across all occurrences.
judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Semantic class for 18/57 empty-limit rows with blank DMR_COMMENT_TEXT and no permit-text match in the packet; per-period applicability of WHEN DISCHARGING rows; whether geometric-mean and pass/fail rows should enter numeric comparison at all; whether report-only classification can be mechanically applied from structured fields without per-parameter permit-text linkage.

proposal.interpretation: Add a row-level empty_limit_semantics classification on permit_limit (and propagated to measurement_limit_pair) using only reusable DMR_COMMENT_TEXT pattern rules: pass_fail_non_numeric when comment contains 'PASS = 0' and 'FAIL = 1'; conditional_discharge when comment contains 'WHEN DISCHARGING'; aggregated_geometric_mean when comment contains 'GEOMETRIC MEAN'; otherwise unresolved_empty_limit. Rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR would be excluded from numeric_comparison_candidate and tagged rather than inferred as numeric limits from LIMIT_TYPE_CODE='ENF'. Report-only monitoring would remain unmapped for rows lacking comment patterns because permit-text linkage is not available in construction.

children.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT encodes PASS=0/FAIL=1 reporting, is the row a numeric concentration limit or pass/fail reporting?
children.resolution: Pass/fail reporting (non-numeric); not an ordinary concentration limit for numeric comparison.

children.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT requires geometric-mean reporting of weekly values, is the row a per-period numeric limit or aggregated report-only monitoring?
children.resolution: Aggregated report-only monitoring per permit footnotes; not a single-period numeric concentration limit in LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.

children.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT is 'WHEN DISCHARGING.', is the row a numeric limit applicable regardless of discharge, or conditionally applicable monitoring?
children.resolution: Conditionally applicable monitoring/reporting; numeric limits for the same parameter may exist on sibling rows, but period-level applicability requires discharge-occurrence evidence not in structured sources.

children.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT is blank, is the row report-only monitoring (per permit Report/N/A columns) or an unclassified data gap?
children.resolution: For rows matched to permit Part I tables showing Report or N/A in the corresponding limit column, report-only monitoring with no numeric limit in that slot; where permit text is not retrieved, remains UNRESOLVED.

refinement.why_necessary: Retrieved evidence shows empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is not semantically uniform across the 57 occurrences. Permit text and structured DMR comments establish at least four materially different obligation types (pass/fail encoding, geometric-mean reporting, when-discharging conditionality, and report-only permit slots with or without sibling numeric limits). A single parent answer would over-generalize and block Purpose A numeric comparison logic differently per partition.
